title: Iterative magnitude pruning based on the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis applied to LXMERT for Visual Question Answering v2.0
content: Iterative magnitude pruning based on the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (which states that a subnetwork retaining the original weight initialization can be trained in isolation to match the full network's accuracy) was applied to the LXMERT model, a two-stream Transformer-based cross-modal vision-and-language model pretrained on image-text pairs, fine-tuned on the VQA v2.0 (Visual Question Answering version 2.0) dataset with the 3,129 most frequent answers as the answer set. The procedure saved the pretrained LXMERT weights plus randomly initialized VQA classifier weights, fine-tuned the model on the answer set, and then performed iterative magnitude pruning by removing the 10% lowest-magnitude weights per iteration across the entire model while excluding the embedding and output layers. After each pruning stage, the original saved weights were restored and the pruned topology was fine-tuned on VQA. This pruning workflow was executed up to roughly 50% sparsity for the main experiments and was evaluated using three different random seeds for the VQA classifier initialization to measure stability.

title: Accuracy of the low-magnitude subnetwork of LXMERT at 50% weight sparsity on the VQA v2.0 task
content: A subnetwork consisting of the 50% lowest-magnitude weights (low-magnitude subnetwork) obtained by iterative magnitude pruning, which iteratively removes the lowest-magnitude weights and restores the original weight initialization before fine-tuning, was applied to the LXMERT model (a two-stream Transformer-based cross-modal model pretrained on image-text pairs) fine-tuned on the VQA v2.0 (Visual Question Answering version 2.0) dataset. After fine-tuning with the pruned topology, this subnetwork attained a mean overall VQA accuracy of 70.72 ± 1.44 on the test-dev split and 70.87 ± 1.51 on the test-std (test-standard) split, which corresponds to approximately 97% of the full fine-tuned LXMERT accuracy of 72.45 on test-dev and 72.63 on test-std. These results are reported as mean ± standard deviation over three random seeds for the VQA classifier initialization.

title: Low-magnitude subnetwork outperforms random and high-magnitude subnetworks at 50% sparsity on VQA v2.0
content: At 50% weight sparsity (i.e., retaining 50% of the weights) and after retraining by fine-tuning with the original weight initialization, for the LXMERT model (a two-stream Transformer-based cross-modal model) fine-tuned on the VQA v2.0 (Visual Question Answering version 2.0) dataset, three equal-sized subnetworks were compared: a low-magnitude subnetwork (consisting of the 50% smallest-magnitude weights), a high-magnitude subnetwork (the complement, consisting of the 50% largest-magnitude weights), and a random subnetwork (a random 50% of weights). The low-magnitude subnetwork substantially outperforms both the high-magnitude and random subnetworks: overall test-dev accuracies are 70.72 ± 1.44 for low-magnitude, 59.35 ± 0.61 for high-magnitude, and 54.86 ± 0.52 for random; analogous test-std (test-standard) accuracies are 70.87 ± 1.51, 59.62 ± 0.55, and 55.19 ± 0.45, respectively. These results are reported as mean ± standard deviation over three random seeds.

title: Model-size cost-benefit analysis for LXMERT on VQA v2.0: accuracy preserved up to 50% sparsity, effective pruning range 40%–60% with 3% accuracy loss
content: For the LXMERT model (a two-stream Transformer-based cross-modal model) fine-tuned on the VQA v2.0 (Visual Question Answering version 2.0) dataset, a model-size cost-benefit study was conducted by applying iterative magnitude pruning (iteratively removing the 10% lowest-magnitude weights across all layers except embedding and output, and restoring the original weight initialization before fine-tuning) from 10% up to 90% sparsity in increments of 10 percentage points, and fine-tuning the pruned network at each sparsity level. The overall VQA accuracy remains relatively preserved up to roughly 40% to 50% sparsity (percentage of weights removed) but suffers a significant decline after approximately 50% to 60% sparsity. Based on these experiments, LXMERT can be effectively pruned by approximately 40% to 60% of its size with about a 3% loss in overall VQA accuracy.

title: Consistency of Lottery Ticket Hypothesis findings for two-stream LXMERT with prior single-stream UNITER results on VQA v2.0
content: For the LXMERT model (a two-stream Transformer-based cross-modal vision-and-language model) fine-tuned on the VQA v2.0 (Visual Question Answering version 2.0) dataset, the existence of trainable low-magnitude subnetworks (obtained by iterative magnitude pruning based on the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis, which retains only the lowest-magnitude weights and restores the original weight initialization for fine-tuning) and their ability to be retrained to near full accuracy are consistent with prior Lottery Ticket Hypothesis findings reported for a single-stream vision-and-language model, UNITER (Universal Image-TExt Representation, a single-stream Transformer-based model). This consistency indicates that magnitude-based Lottery Ticket Hypothesis-style pruning yields sparse, trainable subnetworks in multiple vision-and-language architectures.
